title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel calls (injection + retry semantics)
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Context: multiple customers and internal evals surfaced inconsistent behavior when the model requested multiple tools in parallel: (1) injected tool results could interleave unpredictably with streaming tokens, (2) retries for transient tool failures sometimes replayed user-visible tool output or dropped injections, and (3) multi-tool responses lacked a clear canonical order for injection and structured output compatibility (OpenAI-compatible tool calling).

This PR implements a set of ergonomics improvements to tool/function calling: 1) deterministic injection pipeline that serializes tool-result injection points relative to the model's tool request tokens while preserving streaming stability; 2) a retry orchestration layer that distinguishes idempotent tool calls vs. non-idempotent calls and surfaces retry decisions to the model via a structured metadata event; 3) first-class support for multi-tool parallel calls with consistent ordering semantics and optional per-tool backoff; 4) improved OpenAI-compat compatibility for function/tool calling edge cases (tool_result vs content variants) and structured output mapping; 5) tests, docs, and examples demonstrating parallel tool usage and migration notes.

Key behaviors: deterministic injection: tool results are attached as atomic injection events tied to the model's tool call token index; streaming continues while waiting for long-running tools but will emit a "tool_pending" event to the client if the model advances past the call. Retry semantics: retries for idempotent tools are done transparently; for non-idempotent tools we expose a "retry_suggested" control event and leave the final decision to the calling application. Multi-tool calls: callers can request parallel=true and an ordering policy (response_order: [request_order|completion_order|canonical_tool_order]). Default is request_order to preserve prompt intent. OpenAI compatibility: map legacy "function_call"/"tool_call" variants into a unified representation and include both raw and normalized fields in the API response for gradual migration.

Migration notes: existing callers relying on implicit injection ordering should validate with the new "response_order" flag. Behavior change is opt-in for non-default ordering. The unified function/tool representation is additive and backward compatible for most SDKs; SDK patch releases included in this PR update Python/TS client parsing.

Testing: unit + integration coverage added for parallel tool execution, retry workflows, streaming injection events, and OpenAI compatibility mappings. Load tests exercise 2000 concurrent tool-invoking streams with simulated blocking tools.

Rollout plan: gated feature flag per-tenant, staged rollout to 10% of traffic, monitor injection ordering regressions and latency tail; fallback to previous pipeline on failure.

Related Linear: ENG-1729, ENG-1834. Related PRs: small SDK patches and docs landing in this stack are included as follow-ups.

review_conversation: Reviewer Evan: asked for clearer guarantees when mixing streaming partial tokens with injected tool results; requested an explicit event for 'tool_pending' so clients can show progress. Author (Maya): added 'tool_pending' event and tests. Reviewer Sofia: requested idempotency registry to prevent silent double-effects on retries; asked for an audit event when a non-idempotent retry is suggested. Author: added idempotency registry, surfaced 'retry_suggested' event and audit log hook. Reviewer Liam: asked for SDK parsing consistency and OpenAI compatibility tests. Author: included Python/TS client patches and additional compatibility test cases. All reviewers approved after two rounds of changes.
release_notes: Improved tool calling ergonomics: deterministic injection ordering, streaming-friendly 'tool_pending' events, configurable multi-tool ordering, retry orchestration with idempotency handling, and improved OpenAI-compatible function/tool mappings. SDK updates for Python and TypeScript included.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind tenant flag 'tool_exec_ergonomics_v2'. Monitor metrics: tool_injection_latency_ms, tool_pending_emitted_count, tool_retry_rate, streaming_token_lag_p99. Rollback by disabling flag or reverting to previous pipeline version. Ensure audit-log exporter includes retry_suggested events for compliance-sensitive tenants.
examples_snippet: Example: call tools in parallel via API: {"tools": ["search", "calculator"], "parallel": true, "response_order": "request_order"} -> server emits streaming tokens, emits 'tool_pending' while waiting, then injects tool results as discrete 'tool_result' events tied to call index. SDKs parse combined raw/normalized tool result fields.
qa_summary: QA ran deterministic and randomized fuzz tests for injection order, validated no regressions for single-tool flows, ran load tests with simulated 2k concurrent streams, verified SDK roundtrip parsing. No user-facing regressions observed on canary (10% rollout).
